trial_court: Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class (Central), CC No.3054/2018

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Alka Jain, proprietor of M/s Mayank Trading Company
parties.respondent_defendant: Navank Arora, s/o Sh. Manoj Arora, proprietor of M/s Samsara Enterprises

facts_of_case: Complainant Alka Jain's business partner Navank Arora failed to pay Rs. 16,00,147/- and issued a cheque which was dishonoured. Complainant issued legal notice but the accused did not respond.

legal_principles.principle: The complainant has to prove beyond reasonable doubt elements of Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act.
legal_principles.held: to bring home the guilt of the accused, the complainant has to prove beyond reasonable doubt elements of Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act by crossing the following legal benchmarks

legal_principles.principle: The cheque was drawn by the accused on account maintained by him with the banker for payment of any amount of money out of that account to the complainant.
legal_principles.held: The cheque was drawn by the accused /drawer on account maintained by him with the banker for payment of any amount of money out of that account to the complainant

legal_principles.principle: The complainant has to prove that the cheque was returned unpaid by the bank.
legal_principles.held: The said cheque was returned unpaid by the bank

legal_principles.principle: The complainant has to prove that the cheque was presented before the bank within a period of three months from the date on which it was drawn or within a period of its validity, whichever is earlier.
legal_principles.held: The said cheque was presented before the bank within a period of three months from the date on which it was drawn or within a period of its validity, whenever is earlier

legal_principles.principle: The complainant has to prove that the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, made a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque within 30 days of receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid.
legal_principles.held: The payee or the holder, in due course of cheque, as the case may be, made a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving the notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque within 30 days of receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid

use_for_drafting: drafting a complaint under section 138 NI Act
defending an accused in cheque bounce cases
